Introduction

This document is designed to test text wrapping behavior in the PDF renderer. Each paragraph below contains enough text to force wrapping at the right margin, exercising the word-wrap algorithm across various content patterns.

Paragraph with Inline Formatting

This paragraph contains bold text that spans multiple words and italic text that also spans multiple words as well as monospace code spans like variable_name_with_underscores mixed together. The purpose is to verify that the word-wrapping algorithm correctly handles segments with different font metrics since bold text is wider than regular text and italic text uses oblique variants of the same font family.

Nested Lists with Long Items

  • The first item in this unordered list contains enough text to demonstrate that list items properly wrap at the right margin without overlapping the bullet point or extending beyond the page boundary.

    • A nested item that also contains a substantial amount of text to verify that the indentation is properly applied and the available width for text wrapping is reduced accordingly.

      • A deeply nested item with even more indentation, reducing the available text width further and testing the wrapping behavior under constrained horizontal space.

  • The second top-level item returns to the normal indentation level and continues with more text to ensure consistent behavior across all list nesting levels.
